# **Recontinuation: Production Chains, Economy and Rules**
*Generated by `scripts/gen-prod-guide.js` from `game_config.json` (theme: recontinuation). Do not edit by hand: change the config or the script and regenerate. Names are the theme's; ids are in brackets.* A tick is **15 seconds** by default (`TICK_MS` overrides it).

## **1. Survival drain**
* Start: **20 population**, credits 500. Each person consumes 0.1 Filtrate and 0.1 Nutrient Paste per tick (a starting drain of 2 Filtrate and 2 Nutrient Paste per tick).
* Starting stock: 1500 Reclaim, 50 Aquifer Draw, 80 Filtrate, 100 Nutrient Paste.
* If nobody is making food or water the colony does not die at once: hunger costs morale in proportion to how short it is, people leave rather than starve, and at morale 0 the colony **shuts down** (see section 4b).

## **2. Power is a grid**
Energy is not stockpiled. Each tick, supply (the Core's own power plus generators) is compared with demand (the energy input of everything running). If demand exceeds supply, **every consumer runs at supply/demand efficiency**. Paused and damaged buildings draw nothing. Fuel generators also consume an input and stop without it. **Every district has its own grid.**

## **4b. People, housing, crew, morale and shutdown**
* **Housing.** The population cap is the Core's own quarters (30, 35, 40, 45, 50 at Core levels 1-5) plus homes in any district. Homes in other districts add capacity and comfort only: **everyone eats from the Core stockpile.** If homes are lost, people leave.
* **Growth.** One more person every 3 ticks (two at morale 85+) while morale is 60+, there is room, and the colony can feed them (counting what standing routes bring into or take out of the Core): the surplus must cover the new people, or the stockpile above 60% of capacity must cover the shortfall for 2,000 ticks.
* **Crew.** The workforce is 80% of the population. If there are fewer hands than posts, the essential buildings (water, food, power and salvage) are crewed first and every other staffed building shares who is left, at the same reduced efficiency.
* **Meals** are optional: people eat 0.05 per head per tick; the share fed adds up to **+15** to the morale target.
* **Comfort.** Every building has a comfort effect on adjacent homes, clamped to -15..+8.
* **Morale target** = base 80 + comfort + meals. Morale rises 2 per tick toward it and falls 1 per tick; hunger drops it by up to 10 per tick in proportion to the shortage. Output scales with morale: a slowdown of 1.2% per point below 70 (floor ×0.5) and up to +8% from 85.
* **Exodus.** When short of food or water, 6% of the population leaves each tick, never below 5. Below morale 45, one person leaves every 3 ticks.
* **Shutdown.** The colony no longer collapses. When morale reaches 0 it **shuts down**: every building that is not essential is **parked** (switched off; housing and the Core's essential buildings stay on, everything in other districts is parked), morale is set to 35, and the colony cannot collapse again while shut down. It recovers by itself once nobody is starving and morale is back to 60. Parked buildings stay parked until the player restarts them, all at once ("Restart parked buildings") or one by one. The player can keep rebuilding, or abandon the colony from the menu (two confirmations; progress resets).

## **5b. The work queue**
* **One build slot per place.** The Core, every district, the station and every territory each build one thing at a time. Building, replacing, expanding, upgrading and (in the Core) founding a district all wait in the same line, up to 8 orders per place. Places do not hold each other up.
* **Strict order.** Orders are carried out in the order they were queued. Nothing behind the front of the queue starts early, even if the place could pay for it. A waiting order can be moved up, down or to the front, and cancelled.
* **Paid for when it starts.** An order costs nothing while it waits, so it can be queued before the materials exist. When its turn comes it waits at the front until its place can pay, and everything behind it waits too. Cancelling an order that has started refunds it in full.
* **Dropped orders.** An order that can no longer be carried out when its turn comes (its plot was taken, the building is gone) is taken off the queue with a note in the log.
* **Replace in place.** A building can be swapped for another on the same plot. The order goes through the queue and the old building keeps working until its turn. It is then scrapped for the demolition refund (50%), and the plot stands empty while the new building goes up, which takes **×1.5** its usual build time. Expansion levels are not carried over. A workshop with a recipe set has to be demolished instead.
* **Rush** applies to the order under way, not to one that is waiting.

* **More build slots.** The Core and each district can buy up to 2 more build slots from their hub pane, each paid at once from that place's own stockpile and the treasury. With more slots that many orders from the front of the queue are carried out side by side; the order of the queue is as strict as before, so an order that cannot start yet still holds up everything behind it. The station and territories keep one slot.

## **5c. Alternative recipes**
Most production buildings can be set to another recipe from their pane: a higher-yield way of making the same thing that needs something from further along the chain, or a different product altogether. They stand in for research. A building's alternatives open with the **level of the place it stands in** (the Core's level in the Core, the district's own level elsewhere) or at a colony **milestone**. The base recipe never goes away. Switching costs nothing but leaves the line idle for **10 ticks** while it is retooled, every time.

**District tiers.** A district's tier-1 buildings (Strata Drill, Black Smelter, Pipeline Tap, Cracking Tower, Fuel Turbine, Cliffside Bio Dome, Cliffside Agri Lab) run on what the Core and the district itself make, so a district works even if it is the only one founded; their base recipes also leave a little Reclaim for the district to build with. Tier-2 buildings (Ink Reclaimer, Phononic Fab, Spine Alloy Works, Polymer Plant, HTR Lab) need at most one kind of goods from another district. Tier 3: Klein Cell Forge.
**Standby power.** Klein Reserve Bank: up to 90 power, only while the place's grid is short, burning 1 Klein Cells per tick at full output (in proportion to what it supplies) from that place's stockpile. With nothing to burn it supplies nothing.

## **8. Districts**
Districts unlock at Core level 4. Each has its own stockpile, power grid and rings (capacities 3-5-7-9-11 by level). Level unlocks: district level 2 needs Core level 4; district level 4 needs Core level 5; district level 5 needs Core level 5 and the Beacon.

## **9. Logistics: shipments, routes and links**
* **One-off shipments:** at most 6 on the road at once, up to 300 units each. Stock leaves now and arrives after the trip (anything over the destination's storage cap is lost).
* **Standing routes:** up to 40. A route moves goods directly every tick, limited by the link's capacity and the source's reserve, and shows in both districts' rates. A route can also be given a target: it stops once the destination holds that much (0 = no target: it fills the destination's storage). Routes do not use shipment slots.

## **10. Building expansion**
A building can be expanded in place up to level 5; its whole line scales and its crew grows. Cost is the class base cost × (level - 1), paid from the district's own stockpile. Levels 6-10 stay hidden until the colony's first rare resource has come home to its station (section 16); they also cost the class's orbital goods × 1 (level 6), 2 (level 7), 3 (level 8), 5 (level 9), 8 (level 10), which have to come down from orbit by link or express drop.

## **11. Hazards**
Hazards are forecast, then strike on a fixed tick, then last for a while whatever the outcome. A new hazard is only started while the player is active; once forecast it strikes whether or not they are logged in. At the strike the colony spends its reserves automatically; that gives a preparedness fraction (**prep**), the failure effect applies at severity = 1 - prep, and a maintenance cost applies in proportion to prep. Requirements scale with Core level (+60% per level above 1). The first hazard can come at colony age 45, then every 32-52 ticks, shrinking by 7% per Core level (floor 60%).

| Phantom Drag (equipment_fault) | 1 | 18-28 | 14 | 25 Hard-Spec Parts, 150 Reclaim | buildings degraded |

| Orpheus Cascade (signal_storm) | 5 | 20-28 | 12 | 40 Phononic Circuits, 3 Klein Cells | output cut |
At The Sanctuary Port, a hazard's reserve can be covered by a shield bought with trade goods (see section 14).

## **13. The exchange (order book)**
Unlocks at Core level 4. A ladder of 5 price rungs per resource, filled by simulated traders whose prices follow a deterministic random walk (periods 37, 89, 211 ticks) with occasional shortage and glut events. Other colonies' orders sit on the same book. Matching is price first, then time, at the resting order's price. A 4% fee is taken from sellers; orders expire after 30, 100, 300 ticks; at most 10 open orders per colony. Bids and asks are clamped to a band around the convoy's prices so the exchange cannot be used to beat the convoy for free money. Some resources are price-linked to others (Raw Ink at 0.5 × Polymer Stock).

## **14. The Free Port: trade goods, missions and standing**
Anything can be built here except the extractors of the other districts. Licensed Workshops turn colony goods into trade goods: choose a recipe and it is locked in (changing it costs 30 ticks' worth of output and idles the shop for 20 ticks). A bigger plot runs a bigger batch: Small ×1, Medium ×2, Large ×3.5, Heavy ×5.

## **15. The Beacon**
Build the Series-9 Beacon (only one; it wants a Colossal plot) and keep it running. Each tick it runs at full efficiency adds 1 signal, and **25 signal** completes the transmission. Anything that starves it of power or inputs, or knocks it offline, costs time. Completing it makes The Sanctuary Port available. Once the transmission is complete the Beacon stops burning its inputs and only needs 60 power to stay lit.

## **15b. Settlements**
Once the Beacon has transmitted, camps answer it. 3 are on offer at a time, each of a kind, with a trait and a name, each asking for 600-1500 ticks before it moves on and another takes its place. The colony sponsors one for each of the Beacon, The Sanctuary Port, the station it has. This is where a finished colony's goods go: nothing sent earns credits.
**Steady support.** A sponsored settlement draws its basket from the Core every tick, at the commitment set for it (off, half or full), and never takes a good below the reserve (a share of the Core's storage; 10% unless changed). What it gives back follows what it has actually been getting, averaged over about 40 ticks: half the basket, half the benefit. It also earns standing with its faction, 0.02 a tick per stage at full supply.
**Drives.** Each stage has a drive: the stage's basket 60, 80, 100, 120, 150 times over (stages 1 to 5), given in any amounts at any time. Finishing one moves the settlement up a stage, pays 10 standing per stage and doubles its benefit for 300 ticks. The last drive sets it on its own feet: it leaves its slot, needs nothing more, and is a trade partner for good. A partner goes on giving 20% of what it gave at stage 5 and adds 2% to what the convoy will carry; each further partner counts for 80% of the one before (of its kind for the benefit, of any kind for the convoy), so there is always a reason for one more and never a runaway.
**Appeals.** Every 150-400 ticks a settlement asks for one thing, worth 10-25 ticks of its basket, within 60-160 ticks. Answering doubles its benefit for 120 ticks and pays 4 standing per stage; letting it pass costs nothing.
The discount from all settlements together is capped at 30%. If link room lent by a settlement falls away (it goes short, or a boon runs out), the routes on that link may add up to more than it carries. Routes carrying what people eat and drink keep running in full; the rest are slowed in proportion until the link fits, and each says so. Nothing is cancelled: the routes run at the rate they were set to again as soon as there is room.

## **16. Orbit (endgame)**
Hidden until the colony's standing with all factions adds up to **500** (the Brief only hints at it before then). Then three buildings appear: the Orbital Staging Platform and the Orbital Catapult in the Core, each on its own Colossal plot and side by side, and the Orbital Command Center in The Sanctuary Port on a Heavy plot.
**Launch cycles.** The staging platform takes one cycle at a time and draws its inputs every tick until the progress is complete (only the fully supplied share of a tick counts), then waits. The catapult launches it while the command center is running.
| Cycle | Draws / tick | Ticks | Also costs | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| station | 10 Spine Frames, 10 Dampener Fittings, 10 Donstand-Pattern Modules | 450 | – | the station (named by the player) with 150 Spine Frames, 110 Dampener Fittings, 120 Klein Cells and one dropship |
| ring2 | 12 Spine Frames, 12 Dampener Fittings, 12 Donstand-Pattern Modules | 450 | – | station level 2 |
| ring3 | 15 Spine Frames, 15 Dampener Fittings, 15 Donstand-Pattern Modules | 450 | 60 Sirius Core, 60 Dense Metal | station level 3 |
**Station.** Rings 1: 4 slots of Medium, 2: 6 slots of Large, 3: 9 slots of Heavy; ring 1 at level 1, the others from the ring launches. Base power 10. Klein Reactor: 1 Klein Cells → 90 power. Orbital Foundry: any standard trade recipe at power × 2.5 (clamped 10-60) plus the orbital recipes, no crew.

| Cliffside Rejuvenator (chiral_serum) | 2 Mycolian Spores, 1 Phononic Substrate, 1 HTR Patches, 30 power | 0.25 Cliffside Rejuvenator |

| Stabilized Alloy (still_frames) | 1 Graviton Metaloid, 1 Orphic Silt, 2 Spine Frames, 50 power | 0.25 Stabilized Alloy |
**Orbital storage** is slot-limited: one resource per slot (level 1: 6 slots of 2,000; level 2: 9 slots of 4,000 for 250000 credits, 200 Spine Frames, 120 Dampener Fittings; level 3: 12 slots of 8,000 for 600000 credits, 300 Spine Frames, 200 Dampener Fittings, 30 Stabilized Alloy). The largest stocks claim slots first; anything without a slot is lost. Jettisoning empties a slot, which then costs 20 Spine Frames, 10 Dampener Fittings to rebuild. Headquarters can add high-capacity slots and links on top of these (section 16c).
**Orbital links** run between the Core and the station, both ways (level 1: 4 links at 25/tick; level 2: 6 links at 40/tick for 150000 credits, 200 Dampener Fittings, 100 Donstand-Pattern Modules; level 3: 8 links at 60/tick for 400000 credits, 300 Dampener Fittings, 30 Sirius Cell). Rare resources never travel by link. **Express launch:** up to 400 of one resource from the Core, 150 + 0.5/unit Refined Fuel, arriving in 12 ticks, once every 480 ticks. **Express drop:** the other way, from orbital storage to the Core, for a capsule of 10 Dampener Fittings from orbital storage, landing in 12 ticks; it shares the cooldown.
**Dropships** (up to 3, plus any Headquarters bays; build 300000 credits, 600 Spine Frames, 400 Dampener Fittings, 300 Donstand-Pattern Modules, 200 Klein Cells, 120 ticks): level 1 power 50, hold 600, links 15/tick; level 2 power 80, hold 1000, links 25/tick (250000 credits, 200 Spine Frames, 150 Dampener Fittings, 80 Klein Cells); level 3 power 120, hold 1600, links 40/tick (600000 credits, 350 Spine Frames, 250 Dampener Fittings, 120 Donstand-Pattern Modules); level 4 power 240, hold 3600, links 60/tick (Headquarters refit only; never destroyed). Landing takes 15 ticks with a kit of 140 Hard-Spec Parts, 110 Print Stock, 10 Spine Alloy; the hold can be preloaded. A ship on a territory gets up to 2 links to the station. Recalling brings back what the plan says (rare first) up to the hold, in 150 ticks. Damage costs integrity; repairs cost the ship's value × damage. The first loss is saved at 10% with the cargo gone; the second loses the ship.
**Anomalous territories** are shared by every station: at least 7 are open, a taken one is replaced in 10-30 ticks. Each has two common resources (Reclaim, Aquifer Draw, Raw Ink), one district resource (Raw Ore, Crude) and one rare (Anfang Glass, Icarus Compound, Mobiulic Ore, Windsor Crystal, Mycolian Spores, Orphic Silt, Phononic Substrate, Graviton Metaloid). Rings 1: 3 × Small, 2: 5 × Medium, 3: 7 × Large, storage = the hold, power = the ship's. Leaving early keeps only 35% of its remaining time for the next visitor; still being there when it closes forces a late recall with damage.

## **16c. Headquarters (after the story)**
Opens once the colony has read part 1 of any data packet (a screen beside Data). **Activation** is one bill, paid from the Core (credits from the treasury) in any instalments: 500 Sirius Core, 500 Dense Metal, 500 Sirius Cell, 10000 Spine Frames, 10000 Dampener Fittings, 10000 Donstand-Pattern Modules, 10000 Tool Steel, 10000 Cast Plastics, 100000 Hard-Spec Parts, 100000 Print Stock, 100000 Spine Alloy, 100000 Ingots, 100000 Polymer Stock. After the last delivery the rebuild takes 4320 ticks (18 h). Then the **charter**: 2,000,000 credits, a ◆ after the station's name on the orbital market, and 1 free unlock.
**Unlocks.** One at a time. The player sees which goods an option takes, but not how many until they commit to it. The bill is the category's base × 1.25^n and the work takes 1440 × 1.1^n ticks, where n counts every paid unlock so far (one counter for every category). Committing (or switching) takes 1 data fragment. Abandoning refunds nothing; switching carries 25% of what was delivered across, for the goods both bills share. Free unlocks skip the bill and the wait and do not move the counter. No caps.

| Surface Colony Expansion | 400000 credits, 15000 Print Stock, 20000 Hard-Spec Parts, 1500 Spine Frames, 3000 Cast Plastics, 150 Sirius Core | Standing route slot; District link capacity |
| Territory Deployment Support | 400000 credits, 15000 Refined Fuel, 8000 Polymer Stock, 1500 Apex Field Kits, 300 Heritage Masterworks, 150 Sirius Cell | Territory stabilizer; Stable territory finder; Extra territory link |
| Option | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| Chart a new district | A new district of an existing type, ready to found. The first is a Free Port. |
| Orbital link | +1 Core link. |
| High-capacity storage slot | A storage slot with 10× capacity. Never jettisoned. |
| Dropship bay | +1 dropship. |
| Level 4 dropship refit | A level-3 dropship becomes level 4 and indestructible. |
| Standing route slot | +1 standing route. |
| District link capacity | +50/t on every district link. |
| Territory stabilizer | Take it on a deployment: the territory lasts 100× longer, loses its harm and opens to every station. Reusable. |
| Stable territory finder | A private, long-lived territory whose rare can always be tapped. |
| Extra territory link | Reusable kit: +1 link for a deployed ship. |
Discovered districts lie 2 ticks further out per discovery (one-off shipments take that much longer). A stabilizer multiplies the territory's remaining time by 100 when it lands and cools down for 40320 ticks (168 h) from deployment. A stable territory lasts 500 × the average territory lifetime.
**How the bill grows.** Every amount in a category's base bill is multiplied by the factor below (rounded), and so is the work time.
| Paid unlocks so far (n) | Bill × | Work time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 1 | 1440 ticks (6 h) |
| 1 | 1.25 | 1584 ticks (6.6 h) |
| 2 | 1.56 | 1742 ticks (7.3 h) |

**Details.** A discovery is never founded for you; after the first (a Free Port) its type is random and never the same twice in a row. A stabilised territory keeps its bonuses (rare yield and ship power never fall below ×1, and it does no damage). A stable territory's commons and district resource are chosen so its random rare can be tapped; it has no data site and no anomaly effects. A high-capacity slot holds 10 × the storage level's slot cap. A resource that needs a slot takes an ordinary one first, the player moves goods between the two kinds, and an empty high-capacity slot is freed rather than jettisoned. The level 4 refit can only be chosen while a dropship is at level 3; if that ship is no longer at level 3 when the work finishes, the refit is banked and applied later from the ship card. Level 4 cannot be bought the ordinary way. Several territory link kits can go out with one ship; they are free again once it flies home or is lost. A stabilised territory takes one ship from each station, and a private stable territory takes one ship at a time from the station that found it, as often as it likes. Neither is ever destabilised, and neither counts toward the shared territories kept open.
**Story.** Opening Headquarters plays a call from Seven: the colony is qualified to run independently, but the headquarters is down. The charter plays a second: the commander is now an **Independent Colony Commander**, with the crew still there in support. Headquarters is per player; bots ignore it.

## **16b. Time away and parked colonies**
Only colonies whose commander is around are simulated. "Around" means a real interaction: signing in, opening the game, any action, or any click or key in the game (the page reports input at most every 5 minutes). The live stream and state polls an idle open tab keeps making do not count. A new hazard is only started while the player is active (any request in the last 120 seconds, an open tab included).
| Time since the last interaction | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| up to **96 hours** | Simulated as normal. |
| 96 hours to **30 days** | Not simulated: the colony waits exactly as it was (nothing is taken). The next interaction resumes it, with a one-time notice that it was held. Timers on the shared clock (shipments, express trips, offers) keep running and settle on its first tick back. |
| over 30 days | Parked. On return the commander chooses: **retake** it (it resumes where it stopped), **start a new colony**, or log out. Every action is refused until they choose. |
Starting a new colony does not delete the parked one: it moves, still parked, to a generated account (a random callsign nobody can sign in to) and its station is renamed at random. A parked colony can be handed to another account (`absence.claim`): the bot runner (`npm run bots`, with `BOT_API_KEY`) claims stable parked colonies for bots on small worlds, and gives back any that fail. A commander whose colony was claimed can only start over. Neither can be undone. Open market orders stay open while a colony is frozen or parked and expire as usual. Both limits are `global.absence`.
**Abandon colony** (in the menu) does the same for a healthy colony, one with no collapse countdown that is not shut down or collapsed: it is parked under a generated account for a bot to claim, and the player starts again from the beginning. A colony that is not healthy is erased instead. A brand-new colony counts down until it makes its own water and food, so abandoning one in its first minutes erases it.

## **17. Operations: backups**
The server backs the database up automatically (`BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS`, default 6, 0 = off; `BACKUP_KEEP`, default 28; `BACKUP_DIR`). To restore: stop the server, copy a backup over the database file (delete its `-wal` and `-shm` files), start the server.
